executive_summary: EUR/CHF trades at 0.93244, up 0.88% over one month, 2.39% over three months and 1.70% over six months, sitting at the 76th percentile of a 52-week range bounded by 0.89457 and 0.94453 — a pair that has recovered its entire March collapse and is now grinding at the top of an eighteen-month band. The dominant bilateral narrative is the widest and most one-directional policy gap this cross has carried since 2015: the ECB deposit rate at 2.25% against an SNB policy rate of 0.00% gives +225bp of annualised carry, and the euro leg is scheduled to widen it while the franc leg is administratively frozen, with Bloomberg reporting that the SNB is set to keep rates on hold at 0.00% until the end of 2027 according to people familiar with thinking inside the central bank. The bilateral interaction that neither standalone dossier captures is that the euro's own biggest problem — an energy-driven terms-of-trade tax and a 137.5bp carry deficit to the dollar — is almost entirely absent from this cross, because Switzerland is also a net energy importer and because the franc out-yields nothing: the euro's weakest factor, Policy & Rates, is its strongest factor here. Against that, the two dossiers agree on the direction that hurts this pair: euro-area external balance is deteriorating (current account 1.7% of GDP and falling) while Switzerland runs a 9.77%-of-GDP surplus, and every euro-area fiscal and political risk on the calendar — the 17 November PLF 2027 vote above all — transmits into this cross specifically because the franc is the intra-European flight-to-quality destination. The inflation differential has just widened to roughly 2.5 percentage points, with Swiss inflation at 0.4% in July, the lowest in four months, against euro-area inflation back at 2.9%. We are tactically Bullish at conviction 4 (weighted score +0.4709) targeting 0.9400, and strategically Bullish at only conviction 2 (weighted score +0.1470) targeting 0.9450, the step-down reflecting that the carry and guidance case is fully live now while the Swiss external surplus, the euro fiscal calendar and the persistently negative option skew all gain weight with time. The caveat is explicit: this is a carry-and-policy trade in a 3.4%-volatility pair, and the loss distribution on a franc-haven event has no natural stop.

market_context.valuation_assessment: Both dossiers place this pair almost exactly at fair value on a real-effective basis, and unusually they agree on the sign and roughly on the magnitude. The euro dossier's relative-REER grid puts the euro 0.6% rich against the franc, implying EUR/CHF fair value of 0.9261 — the tightest real-effective relationship in its entire G10+SGD set. The franc dossier's mirror calculation gives a -0.97% deviation and an implied 0.9227. Spot at 0.93244 is therefore roughly 0.2-1.1% above the two independent fair-value estimates — inside noise, and not a valuation constraint. The Swiss REER at 101.69 sits at only the 40th percentile of its window, so there is no franc overvaluation to mean-revert; the euro REER at 102.69 is 0.5% above its own mean, so there is no euro cheapness to harvest either. The valuation channel is genuinely dormant for this cross, which leaves rates, flows and terms of trade to set direction — and that is the specific reason the carry differential dominates the weighted score.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The carry differential is +225bp annualised in favour of a long EUR/CHF position, scheduled to widen rather than narrow: a 25bp ECB hike on 10 September is priced at 77-83% and the cumulative probability of a deposit rate above 2.25% by 17 December is 91.9%, while the SNB's own June conditional inflation forecast is explicitly constructed on a 0% policy rate across the entire 2026-28 horizon. Front-end reality is wider still — SARON fixed at -0.04% and the SNB lowered its sight-deposit threshold factor from 15 to 13.5 effective 1 August — and term-structure carry is the widest positive spread the euro enjoys against any currency, with the 10Y Bund yielding 268bp more than the 10Y Swiss Confederation bond. Carry-to-volatility at +0.60 is the best in the G10, ahead of long USD/CHF at +0.54, and versus -0.24 for EUR/USD and -0.26 for EUR/AUD — EUR/CHF is the only cross in the euro complex where the euro earns carry at low volatility rather than paying carry at moderate volatility. The carry regime is working and working for this pair: VIX at 17.09, tight credit spreads, low pair implied volatility, and a 225bp differential together create the precise configuration in which funding-currency shorts are scalable at high leverage across the street. The forward curve already agrees with the direction of the differential, with the annualised discount rising from 2.25% to 2.63% across tenors as it embeds further ECB tightening against a static SNB.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The differential is +225bp and its direction of travel is one-way, which is a materially different situation from the euro's other crosses. In EUR/USD the September ECB hike is fully priced at 77-83% and therefore generates no tactical signal, because the dollar leg can also move — the 29 July FOMC held 9-3 with all three dissents favouring a hike. In EUR/CHF the quote leg cannot move at all: the SNB does not meet until 24 September, outside the tactical window, and its own published forecast conditions on zero through 2028. So the same priced ECB hike that is neutral for EUR/USD is bullish for EUR/CHF, because here it is the entire differential. The trajectory compounds: 225bp today, 250bp on a September delivery, and a 91.9% cumulative probability of being above 2.25% by 17 December. The transmission mechanism is the cleanest in FX — 225bp of positive carry at 3.43% implied volatility gives the highest carry-to-vol ratio in the G10 at +0.60, which makes the pair the market's default funding expression and produces persistent mechanical selling of francs against euros irrespective of news. The residual mispricing is on the Swiss side: roughly 12-25bp of hawkish SNB premium still embedded in the CHF front end against a central bank whose sell-side consensus is 28 of 29 forecasters expecting no change through 2026. Each basis point of that premium decaying is a pair-positive with no offsetting mechanism.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months this is the strongest single argument in the report and it is where the two dossiers reinforce most cleanly: the euro dossier turns Policy & Rates strategically Bullish because the ECB's trajectory is favourable for the first time in three years, and the franc dossier turns it strategically Bearish CHF because every peer is tightening while the SNB has removed itself as a variable. Applied bilaterally, the differential widens from 225bp toward 250-275bp by year-end on published paths, and there is no scenario inside the horizon in which the Swiss leg contributes to narrowing it — the SNB's base case maintains the policy rate at 0% with the Governing Board characterising current settings as appropriately expansionary. The real-rate comparison sharpens it further: the euro area's 2.25% policy rate against 2.9% HICP is a real rate of -0.65%, while Switzerland's 0.00% against 0.4-0.5% CPI is roughly -0.45% — nominally similar in real terms, which is precisely why the nominal differential does the work in a carry trade financed at nominal rates. The forward curve already embeds part of this, with the annualised discount rising from 2.25% at one month to 2.63% at six months, so our edge is not the direction of the differential but its magnitude: we expect 0.9450 at six months against a computed 6M forward of 0.92021, a 248-pip gap. Confidence is 75 rather than higher because the strategic window contains two SNB assessments plus a December Monetary Policy Report, each of which could reprice the Swiss curve if energy pass-through proves stickier than the 0.6% forecast — and because BNP Paribas expects the SNB to begin normalising in Q3 2027, outside our horizon but a sign of how the market would begin to front-run it.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation differential is the widest in years and it moved further apart in the last week of July, which is unambiguously pair-bullish inside four weeks. The Federal Statistical Office released Swiss inflation at 0.4% in July, the lowest in four months, while Eurostat announced euro-area inflation back at 2.9%, taking the gap to 2.5 points — the fuel behind the divergence between an ECB the market expects to hike as soon as September and an SNB anchored at 0.00%. Composition matters and it also favours the pair: euro-area core HICP rose to 2.5% and services to 3.3% with all four components accelerating, while the SNB's preferred core measure is 0.3% — a core differential of roughly 2.2 percentage points. On growth the two economies are closer than the inflation gap suggests, with euro-area Q2 GDP at +0.4% q/q against Swiss Q1 at +0.4% q/q, but the asymmetry in the data calendar is decisive: euro-area releases carry higher pair beta because they move the ECB's path, whereas Swiss releases can only move an SNB that has pre-committed. The one Swiss release with real pair beta is CPI, and it works in the pair's favour because a soft print revives negative-rate speculation rather than tightening speculation. Which economy's data moves this pair more is therefore settled: euro-area HICP and PMI are the high-beta inputs, and Swiss CPI matters only for its downside.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the differential narrows by construction, and that is the honest reason this factor cannot carry a strategic bullish stance. The euro-area inflation impulse is cost-push: energy at +10.0% y/y is doing almost all the work, the ex-energy rate is 2.2% and unchanged, food has decelerated to 1.2%, the ECB's own wage tracker sits at 2.3% for 2026 with no second-round effects visible, and June projections have HICP peaking at 3.4% in Q3-Q4 2026 before falling to 2.3% in 2027. Swiss inflation, meanwhile, is more likely to drift up than down from 0.4% on the same energy pass-through, with the SNB having already revised its conditional forecast up to 0.6/0.6/0.7 from 0.5/0.5/0.6. Put together, a 2.5pp differential today plausibly becomes 1.6-1.8pp by early 2027 — still large, but narrowing, which removes the incremental support. On growth the asymmetry reverses against the pair: the SNB held at 0.00% at its 18 June assessment for the fourth consecutive time, so Switzerland's growth drag from the 15% Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff does not translate into policy easing and therefore does not weaken the franc through the rate channel — it is a real-economy hit with no monetary transmission. Two forces of roughly equal magnitude, in opposite directions, at a reduced 0.08 weight: a genuine Neutral.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: EUR/CHF is a moderate-risk-sensitivity pair in the framework's classification, and the classification is currently well behaved: the franc is a genuine haven, the euro is explicitly not one, so the pair carries a positive beta to global risk appetite. The current regime is squarely supportive — VIX 17.09, US IG OAS 81bp and HY OAS 281-284bp near cycle tights, S&P 500 at 7,489.72 and the STOXX Europe 600 at a record 655.45. The cleanest bilateral cross-asset signal is gold, because the franc and gold share a debasement-and-uncertainty demand function while the euro has no such linkage: XAU/USD at 4,054.45 is down 12.14% over three months and 17.94% over six from the February peak of 5,277.88, which is direct evidence that the haven complex is being liquidated. The transmission is asymmetric: the euro's own risk exposures express through the terms-of-trade channel rather than the risk-appetite channel, and Switzerland shares the energy-importer status, so on the pure risk-sentiment axis the franc's haven premium deflating is the dominant effect. The most instructive observation is the July test: Brent rose 26% on Hormuz re-escalation and the pair rose 0.88% anyway, because the market classified the energy move as an inflation story that raises the ECB's path rather than a risk story that bids the franc. That classification is one headline from being revised, which is why confidence is 60 rather than 70.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the risk channel is genuinely two-sided for this pair and it is the factor most likely to invalidate the whole thesis, which is why we resolve it Neutral rather than carrying the tactical Bullish forward. The base case is regime persistence, in which the franc's reassignment from haven to funding currency is structural rather than cyclical and the pair grinds higher on carry alone. The bear path is specific and quantifiable: HY spreads at 281-284bp against a 3.63% effective funds rate leave essentially no cushion, and the franc's haven behaviour has two features that distinguish it from the yen — it reacts more slowly but holds its gains longer, because it is driven by capital flight rather than carry unwind. At 3.77% three-month implied volatility the funding trade is carried at very high leverage across the street, so a doubling of realised volatility forces deleveraging through a narrow exit, and the historical template for a funding-currency unwind is a 3-4% move in a fortnight — roughly 300-370 pips on this cross, which would erase more than eighteen months of carry. The offsetting consideration is that the SNB's intervention pledge is one-directional: it has committed to selling francs into rapid and excessive appreciation, which caps but does not reverse a haven-driven rally. Two large, opposed, unquantifiable-in-timing forces at a 0.05 weight: Neutral at 50.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At one to six months positioning inverts its own signal on both legs and nets to nothing. A 0th-percentile euro leveraged short is a two-week catalyst and a meaningless six-month one — by definition it cannot get more extreme and will be flat or reversed before the horizon closes. What survives on the base leg is the euro asset-manager long of 228,927 contracts, reducing at roughly 26,000 contracts per four weeks, which is a persistent supply overhang. What survives on the quote leg is the structural franc-funding book, which is far larger than the CME shows and which is a persistent pair-supportive flow. Layered on both is a genuinely bilateral flow that neither dossier captures: Swiss institutional hedging behaviour. Swiss pension funds are structurally the largest private cross-border investor base relative to GDP, and their euro hedging decisions are a direct EUR/CHF flow — foreign currency bonds are usually fully hedged while equities are partially hedged, with the share of unhedged foreign currencies averaging approximately 17% of total assets, meaning any increase in Swiss allocations to euro assets arrives with a mechanical EUR/CHF sell attached through the hedge. Two developments point pair-negative here: Swiss pension funds began reducing or exiting foreign currency government bonds including euro-denominated debt, and Swiss schemes have been allowed since 12 June to undertake repo transactions directly, a mechanical easing of the constraint on maintaining hedges. Net across all four flows: no strategic edge.

The corroborating tell is that franc shorts were being reduced even as the franc weakened in July, which can only be explained by non-futures flow — meaning the visible positioning data understates rather than overstates the crowding risk, and a euro short-covering rally has genuine fuel behind it while a franc short-covering rally does not.

strategic.combined_positioning_signal: The tactical squeeze signal resolves and inverts: the euro asset-manager long overhang (228,927 contracts, reducing ~26,000/4wk) and Swiss pension hedging flows both introduce fresh euro-leg supply, while the unmeasurable franc-funding book remains the dominant but unquantifiable pair-supportive flow
strategic.unwind_trigger: A reduction in euro-area allocations by Swiss pension funds, or a broad deleveraging of the franc-funding carry trade triggered by a volatility spike
strategic.historical_analogue: The euro's share of allocated global reserves fell to 20.03% in 2026Q1 from 20.38%, a second consecutive decline, echoing prior episodes where reserve-manager euro demand faded gradually rather than abruptly
strategic.contrarian_case: The market prices the franc-funding trade as riskless and the euro reserve story as a structural bid, and both are wrong at the margin. A large share of the street holds the same short-franc position through the same low-volatility instrument, so if a shock forces a simultaneous unwind, the exit is far narrower than the aggregate visible position size implies — the contrarian risk is precisely that the position looks uncrowded on the CME while being extremely crowded in the unmeasured funding market.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The external-balance differential is the largest single pair-negative in this report and it is not close: Switzerland runs a current-account surplus of 9.77% of GDP against the euro area's 1.7% and falling — a gap of roughly 8 percentage points of GDP, and one that is widening because the euro-area surplus is eroding (from 2.0% a year ago, with the goods surplus down from EUR350bn to EUR286bn and the monthly goods balance at a EUR7.8bn deficit in May against a EUR15.0bn surplus a year earlier) while the Swiss surplus is merely narrowing at the margin. Switzerland also carries a net international investment position of CHF 974bn against a euro area that is a marginal net creditor. The bilateral trade channel, however, runs the other way: on IMF DOTS data the euro area exported $195.8bn of goods to Switzerland in 2024 against $139.5bn of imports, a net euro-area goods surplus of $56.3bn — roughly $4.7bn per month of structural euro buying and franc selling through the trade channel. So the bilateral goods relationship is pair-positive while the aggregate external positions are strongly pair-negative, and the aggregate dominates because Switzerland's surplus is generated overwhelmingly outside the goods channel and outside the euro area, in services, primary income and non-EU trade, and is recycled abroad as portfolio outflow rather than absorbed domestically. Inside four weeks neither effect transmits with force — current-account data is quarterly and the next Swiss balance-of-payments release falls in late September — so the stance is Bearish at only 55.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.16 weight this is the second-heaviest factor and it is the reason the strategic conviction is 2 rather than 4. Applying the framework's direction rules: oil up → mild-to-moderate negative for the euro (a large net importer; energy HICP +10.0% y/y), while Switzerland is also a net energy importer but with far lower energy intensity and near-zero pass-through (Swiss CPI 0.4% with core 0.3% despite Brent up 26% in a month), so the net effect of a 10% oil rise is EUR/CHF falling roughly 0.4-0.7%. Natural gas (TTF) up → strongly negative for the euro, with TTF at EUR58.62/MWh, +36% on the month and +66% year-on-year, hitting the import bill and current account directly while Switzerland's hydro/nuclear electricity mix insulates it — a 20% TTF rise is worth roughly -0.5% to -1.0% on the pair. Gold up → positive for the franc through the shared haven demand function with no euro linkage, so a 10% gold rally is worth roughly -0.5% to -0.8% on the pair; gold's 17.94% six-month drawdown has been worth roughly +1.0% to +1.4% of pair support, the single largest commodity tailwind the pair has had. Netting the current configuration: gas and oil are pair-negative and gold is pair-positive, roughly offsetting through the summer — but the balance breaks decisively negative into winter, because EU gas storage is 49-55% full against a ten-year average and roughly 10 percentage points behind last year, the balance-of-summer TTF contract trades EUR2.68/MWh over Winter 26/27, Kpler's base case has Hormuz LNG transit constrained through end-2026, and the full EU ban on Russian LNG imports takes effect at end-2026. Three independent supply constraints land in December on the euro leg with no Swiss counterpart. The Swiss offset — the pharma tariff and the USD 200bn Swiss corporate US investment pledge — compresses the Swiss surplus by perhaps 1-2pp of GDP over several years, leaving it above 8% and still four to five times the euro area's. Level dominates change.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: The guidance divergence on this specific pair is unusually decisive: one central bank has published an explicit hawkish reaction function while the other has published a three-year commitment to inaction plus a one-directional intervention pledge — a combination that does not exist in any other euro cross

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the cleanest bilateral factor in the report. The ECB's 23 July statement retained rates but asserted that the risks to the inflation outlook are to the upside, Lagarde disclosed that the unanimous hold masked governors asking whether a hike should be considered, the June Account records that under no scenario would maintaining a 2% deposit rate have been appropriate, and Schnabel has stated publicly that rates are not yet restrictive. The SNB's guidance runs in precisely the opposite direction and is more binding: its conditional inflation forecast conditions on 0% through 2028, and Bloomberg reports suggest the SNB may keep rates at 0.00% until 2027, with the SNB appearing comfortable with the inflation outlook and standing ready to sell francs only against excessive appreciation. That last clause is the crux, and it is a structural asymmetry unique to this cross: the SNB is a committed seller of francs into pair weakness and has no stated response to pair strength. Bilaterally that means the pair has an official floor and no official ceiling. UBS explicitly notes that the SNB may sell francs and purchase euros to counter the franc's overvaluation, which it attributes to transitory safe-haven demand rather than robust Swiss fundamentals. The tactical constraint is that market pricing has largely absorbed both messages, so guidance can now only disappoint — which is why confidence is 68 rather than 80.

tactical.what_is_priced: The market prices a hawkish ECB at 77-83% for September and a frozen SNB, so both sides of the guidance differential are largely in the price. What is not priced is the asymmetry of the SNB's reaction function — the market treats intervention risk as symmetric two-way volatility when the pledge is explicitly one-directional.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the credibility differential matters more than the immediate signal, and it favours the pair on three counts. First, both central banks are highly credible and both are credibly pointing the same direction for this cross — the ECB toward tightening with an explicit published reaction function, the SNB toward permanent inaction with a forecast comfortably inside its band at every horizon. A market that believes both prices a persistently widening differential, which lowers the risk premium on the carry trade and makes the position scalable. Second, the ECB has two dated projection rounds inside the window at which its own arithmetic can force the curve higher, while the SNB's two assessments can only confirm zero or — the genuine two-sided risk — revise the conditional forecast. Third, and most importantly for a strategic view, the SNB's guidance has converted the franc from a currency with policy optionality into one with none, and a currency without optionality that also carries the lowest yield in its peer group is definitionally a funding currency. The SNB held rates at 0% for a second consecutive time in December, reinforcing the view that it will not return to negative rates but will remain on hold and keep the option to intervene in FX markets by selling the franc. The counterweight, and it is why confidence is 70 rather than 80: the SNB is a three-person Governing Board meeting four times a year with no published vote split and no forward guidance, and January 2015 established that its surprises are discontinuous. The strategic bullish case rests on the SNB continuing to do nothing, which is highly likely and completely un-hedgeable.

The unpriced second-order consequence is that a permanently zero SNB makes the franc a structural rather than cyclical funding currency, a multi-year re-rating of the pair's equilibrium level.

factors.horizon_split: Both horizons are Bullish and confidence rises from 68 to 70, which is deliberate. Tactically the guidance differential is fully absorbed by the market and can only disappoint. Strategically the value is institutional rather than informational: two credible central banks committed to opposite courses, four dated communication events, and an intervention pledge that puts an official floor under the pair and nothing over it. The weight uplift from 0.09 to 0.14 nearly doubles the factor's contribution.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The event calendar is asymmetric against this pair, and the asymmetry is specific: every euro-area risk on the calendar transmits into EUR/CHF with higher beta than into any other euro cross, because the franc is the intra-European flight-to-quality destination. Two conflicts sit on Europe's energy supply routes — the Strait of Hormuz largely blocked with Iranian interdictions on 30-31 July, a Houthi Red Sea blockade, and Russian anti-ship strikes off Odesa — and Switzerland is insulated from all of them in a way no euro-area member is. A third and newer vector is transatlantic: the Commission's roughly USD 1bn DMA fine on Google, the Section 301 investigation, and a 15% EU tariff ceiling that is politically rather than legally secure. Against that, the Swiss-side event is dated and pair-positive but almost entirely spent: the Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff at a 15% capped rate took effect on 31 July for Annex III companies, and the tariff was negotiated, capped and pre-announced. Netting a spent, capped Swiss negative against a live, uncapped European negative gives a Bearish stance — but at only 55 confidence and a 0.05 weight, because no single event is likely to fire inside four weeks and because pair implied volatility of 3.43% means the options market is pricing essentially no event premium in either direction.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: The strategic event calendar densifies and every material item skews against the pair. Three clusters matter. The European political cluster is the largest: the German state elections in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Berlin on 20 September with the AfD polling ahead in the former, the French Senate elections on 27 September, and above all the French PLF 2027 sequence from the 30 September Conseil des ministres through the 20 October Part I vote to the 17 November solemn vote on the whole bill, assigned a 20-25% probability of a censure-and-dissolution path. That date is the single largest identified binary for this pair, and its transmission is specifically bilateral: a French fiscal crisis is a euro-wide event whose capital-flight destination is Switzerland, so an OAT-Bund move through 100bp historically drags the euro 1.0-1.5% lower and this pair further than most because the franc is the receiving currency. The energy cluster lands in December — constrained Hormuz LNG transit, EU storage roughly 10 percentage points behind, and the full Russian LNG ban at end-2026 — hitting the euro leg with no Swiss counterpart. The Swiss cluster is small and mixed: the tariff extends to all importers on 29 September and the SNB assessments are genuinely two-sided. The single upside tail is a Russia-Ukraine settlement, worth 1.5-2.5% on this pair, at 15% probability inside six months. Balance clearly negative.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: On this specific pair the fiscal differential is an active transmission channel rather than a background fact: Switzerland is the destination for euro-area fiscal-stress capital flight, so a sovereign event on the base leg moves this cross more than any other euro cross

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The fiscal differential is the widest in the developed world and it points against the pair. Switzerland is AAA across all agencies with general government debt of 37.6% of GDP and a constitutionally entrenched debt brake in force since 2003; the euro area carries aggregate gross debt of 88.9% of GDP (EA21) and rising, with France at 117.5% and a 5.1% deficit, Italy at 138.9%, and the French 10Y OAT at 3.98% having hit a 17-year high twice in July. The bilateral significance is not the level but the direction of the flow it generates: OAT-Bund at 81-82bp now trades at or through BTP-Bund at 80-81bp, an inversion of the euro area's historical credit hierarchy, and the franc is where the marginal euro of European fiscal-risk capital goes. The Swiss 10Y at 0.475% against the Bund at 3.15% is a 268bp quality discount that the market has fully capitalised in bonds and has not capitalised in the currency — the pair sits at the 76th percentile of its 52-week range while the credit differential is at its widest of the cycle. Tactically, however, nothing is dated: the French budget process does not open until 30 September and the only calendar item inside four weeks is the Fitch review of France on 28 August. Bearish at 55 because the level of stress is elevated and rising while the tactical calendar is nearly empty.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the French budget calendar dominates and it is unambiguously pair-negative. The PLF 2027 goes to the Conseil des ministres on 30 September, the Part I solemn vote falls on 20 October and the vote on the whole bill on 17 November; the 2026 budget required Article 49.3 and survived censure motions, and a Bercy-commissioned report dated 15 July warns the deficit could reach 5.9% of GDP in 2027. A successful censure means dissolution and snap legislative elections weeks before a presidential campaign in which Bardella polls at 35%. The bilateral transmission is the sharpest available: an OAT-Bund move through 100-130bp revives the redenomination premium that the Transmission Protection Instrument has never been tested against, and a redenomination premium is by construction a franc-buying event, because the franc is the only European currency that cannot be redenominated. Layered on that is record supply — German 2026 issuance revised up to roughly EUR521.5bn, EU joint borrowing of EUR180bn, and a German 2027 draft budget carrying EUR109.7bn of defence — against a Swiss Confederation that issues sparingly and has no supply problem at all. The offset is genuine but partial: German fiscal expansion raises Bund yields, which widens the Bund-Confederation spread and supports the pair through the rate channel. Net of a live French binary, four French rating reviews inside the window, and 88.9% aggregate debt against 37.6%, this is a clear strategic negative at nearly double its tactical weight.

Spot 0.93244 sits above the 50-day SMA (0.92534), the 100-day (0.92088) and the 200-day (0.91835), the averages are stacked bullishly, and the higher-highs/higher-lows structure has been intact since the 15 March low of 0.89457 — four successively higher swing lows against successively higher highs. Web-sourced levels frame the immediate battle precisely: the pair has cleared the 0.9312-0.9315 resistance zone and the 0.93304 confirmation level, with the next objectives at 0.9350 and 0.9379. The long-term outlook stays bearish as long as 0.9407 — the 2022 low turned resistance — holds; a firm break of 0.9407 would argue that the downtrend from the 1.2004 2018 high has completed with five waves down to 0.8979, with a stronger rebound then seen toward the 38.2% retracement at 1.0135 in the medium term. So 0.9407 plus the 52-week high at 0.94453 form a 40-pip band that is simultaneously the ceiling of our base case and the gateway to a multi-year regime change — the pair's strategic distribution is genuinely bimodal around it, which is why the stance is Neutral rather than Bullish. Against the bullish structure sits the vol surface: the term structure rises smoothly to 4.85% at one year with no kink around the November-December event cluster, and the skew deepens monotonically to -0.74 — the market expects higher variance with a franc-strength bias. Structure constrains rather than directs.

A hawkish Account pushes September pricing from 77-83% toward 90%, which on this cross translates directly into a wider carry differential because the quote leg cannot respond. Unlike EUR/USD, where a hawkish Account competes with a hawkish-dissenting Fed, here it is unopposed.

catalysts.event: Fitch scheduled sovereign rating review of France
catalysts.rationale: Fitch holds France at A+ with a Stable outlook against a 5.1% deficit and 117.5% debt, and an outlook change to Negative ahead of the PLF 2027 process is live. The bilateral transmission is that French fiscal stress is a euro-wide event whose flight-to-quality destination is Switzerland, so this pair carries higher beta to OAT-Bund than any other euro cross. A move from 82bp toward 95-100bp is worth roughly 0.3-0.5% of pair downside.

The decisive input for the 10 September ECB decision, and the single highest-beta release for this pair inside the tactical window. July printed 2.9% headline, 2.5% core, 3.3% services and 10.0% energy, all accelerating. A print at or above 2.9% locks the September hike and takes the differential to 250bp; at or below 2.6% it cuts hike odds below 55% and invalidates the tactical thesis. The franc leg has no equivalent release with comparable policy consequence.

July printed 0.4%, the lowest in four months, against euro-area inflation at 2.9%, taking the differential to 2.5 points. The asymmetry is that a soft Swiss print revives negative-rate speculation and collapses the residual 12-25bp SNB hawkish premium (pair-bullish), while a print above 0.8% would force a genuine 2027 SNB repricing (pair-bearish) — and the SNB has already revised its conditional forecast up once, so the upside risk to Swiss inflation is real.

The first quarter capturing the full trade-uncertainty effect preceding the pharmaceutical tariff, with Q2 real export growth at only +0.6% against +8.8% nominal. A print below 0.2% q/q corroborates EY's 0.6% annual growth forecast against the SNB's 'around 1%' and reinforces the case that the franc's fundamentals no longer justify its level — though weak Swiss growth does not translate into SNB easing, so the transmission is through sentiment rather than rates.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision plus staff projections, hosted by the Bundesbank in Berlin
catalysts.rationale: The single most important dated event for this pair. A 25bp hike to 2.50% is 77-83% priced and takes the differential from 225bp to a permanent 250bp — and this is where the pair diverges most sharply from EUR/USD: a delivered hike is a sell-the-fact for spot in both, but only here does it permanently improve the carry, because the quote leg cannot respond. The projections carry the larger information content: a 2026 HICP revision toward 3.2% with 2027 held at or above 2.3% forces the curve higher.

catalysts.event: SNB Monetary Policy Assessment and news conference
catalysts.rationale: The identified inflection point for the whole thesis and the only scheduled event that can move the franc leg. The SNB revises its conditional inflation forecast — currently 0.6/0.6/0.7 and conditioned on 0% throughout — for the first time since the energy shock re-intensified. An upward revision above 0.9% for 2027 validates the residual market hawkishness and is pair-bearish; a downward revision toward 0.4% revives negative-rate speculation and is pair-bullish. Watch equally for any change to the one-directional 'increased willingness to intervene' language, which is the pair's official floor.

catalysts.event: German state elections in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Berlin
catalysts.rationale: The highest-salience German political event of the autumn, with the AfD polling ahead in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, arriving as the Merz coalition passes a 2027 draft budget carrying EUR109.7bn of defence spending. The bilateral transmission is that questions about the durability of the German fiscal expansion undermine Bund yields, which narrows the 268bp Bund-Confederation spread that underpins this pair's term-structure carry.

catalysts.event: Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs extend to all non-Annex-III Swiss importers
catalysts.rationale: The 15% capped rate took effect 31 July for the seventeen Annex III companies and captures all remaining importers from this date; pharmaceuticals are Switzerland's largest export category to the United States. This is the point at which the drag becomes economy-wide, striking directly at the goods component of the 9.77% current-account surplus that is the pair's principal structural drag. Largely priced, because it was negotiated, capped and pre-announced.

catalysts.event: French PLF 2027 and PLFSS 2027 presented to the Conseil des ministres
catalysts.rationale: The formal opening of the euro's dominant autumn risk and the start of the strategic fade phase. The 2026 budget required Article 49.3 and survived censure motions; the Bercy expert report of 15 July warns of a 5.9% deficit in 2027. On this cross specifically, the transmission is capital flight — the franc is the only European currency that cannot be redenominated, so a French fiscal crisis is mechanically a franc bid rather than merely a euro sale.

catalysts.event: Moody's scheduled sovereign rating review of France
catalysts.rationale: France is Aa3 with a NEGATIVE outlook, and the review falls three days after the 20 October solemn vote on Part I of the PLF 2027, giving Moody's a fresh read on political capacity to consolidate. A downgrade to A1 would be the fourth agency action in thirteen months and would take OAT-Bund toward 100bp — the level at which the euro historically loses 1.0-1.5% and this pair more, given the franc's receiving role.

catalysts.event: French Assemblée nationale solemn vote on the PLF 2027 as a whole
catalysts.rationale: The largest identified binary for this pair in the entire report. If Article 49.3 is used without a negotiated compromise, censure follows; success means dissolution and snap legislative elections weeks before a presidential campaign in which Bardella polls at 35%. Probability of the censure-and-dissolution path is 20-25%, taking OAT-Bund from 82bp toward 130bp. The bilateral mechanism is the revival of a redenomination premium that the Transmission Protection Instrument has never been tested against, and a redenomination premium is by construction a franc-buying event — this is the pair's principal downside scenario.

catalysts.event: SNB Monetary Policy Assessment plus December Monetary Policy Report
catalysts.rationale: The SNB's most information-rich event of the year and the point at which any residual market hawkishness in the CHF front end is either paid or extinguished. It also falls immediately before the December year-end cross-currency basis turn, compounding volatility for a franc-funded book at exactly the moment its funding cost peaks and pair liquidity thins.

catalysts.event: ECB decision plus Eurosystem staff projections; European Council 17-18 December
catalysts.rationale: The market prices a 91.9% cumulative probability of a deposit rate above 2.25% by this date, and a delivered second hike takes the differential to 275bp permanently against a quote leg that will have restated zero a week earlier. The projection round extends meaningfully into 2029 and is the last dated opportunity inside the horizon for the ECB's own arithmetic to force the curve higher.

catalysts.event: Full EU ban on Russian LNG imports takes effect; year-end cross-currency basis turn
catalysts.rationale: A self-imposed euro-area supply cut landing in the same month as constrained Hormuz LNG transit and storage roughly 10 percentage points behind, with no Swiss counterpart because Switzerland's electricity mix is predominantly hydro and nuclear. Simultaneously the year-end basis turn raises the cost of a franc-funded position at its thinnest-liquidity moment. Two independent pair-negatives coinciding on one date, neither visible in the vol term structure.

catalysts.event: SNB sight deposits of domestic banks (weekly, Mondays)
catalysts.rationale: The only high-frequency window into SNB behaviour between quarterly meetings, and it moves this pair specifically. When the SNB sells francs to weaken the currency it credits francs to commercial-bank sight-deposit accounts, so a sharp rise typically signals intervention; week-over-week changes are more informative than the absolute level, though the signal is imperfect and clearer at quarterly horizons, and increases can also reflect the expiration of SNB bills or the non-rollover of repos.

catalysts.event: DBRS and Scope scheduled sovereign rating reviews of France
catalysts.rationale: Two agency reviews on the same day, with Scope already at AA- with a negative outlook heading into the review; a downgrade adds to the fourth-agency-action count inside thirteen months and pressures OAT-Bund ahead of the 20 October PLF vote, transmitting into this cross via the franc's receiving-currency role.

catalysts.event: S&P scheduled sovereign rating review of France
catalysts.rationale: The final scheduled French rating review of the year, falling ten days after the 17 November PLF solemn vote and therefore informed by its outcome; a downgrade compounds any post-vote OAT-Bund widening into year-end, precisely when this pair's liquidity is thinning ahead of the basis turn.

invalidators.condition: EUR/CHF closes below the 50-day SMA at 0.92534 on a daily basis and below the 100-day at 0.92088 on a weekly basis
invalidators.mechanism: The bullish MA stack and the four-swing higher-lows sequence since 15 March are the flow reinforcement that converts a 225bp carry differential into a directional trend — without them the pair reverts to a range in which carry is collected but spot goes nowhere, and Factor 9 flips from Bullish to Bearish, removing +0.0300 and taking the tactical score to +0.4109
invalidators.monitor_indicator: EUR/CHF daily and Friday closes versus 0.92534 and 0.92088

invalidators.condition: The Swiss-euro area headline inflation differential compresses below 1.5 percentage points (Swiss CPI at or above 1.0% with core above 0.6% while euro-area HICP falls below 2.5%)
invalidators.mechanism: This is the only configuration in which the 225bp differential can actually narrow rather than widen. Factor 1 would flip from Bullish 72/75 to Bearish and Factor 2 from Bullish/Neutral to Bearish, swinging the tactical score by roughly -0.51 and the strategic by roughly -0.42, taking both decisively negative
invalidators.monitor_indicator: SFSO Swiss CPI headline and Core inflation 1 versus Eurostat euro-area flash HICP and HICPX
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Monthly, both in the first days of each month

invalidators.condition: The ECB holds all three rates on 10 September against 77-83% pricing AND revises its 2027 HICP projection to 2.1% or below
invalidators.mechanism: The differential would be capped permanently at 225bp with the SNB pinned at zero — carry would still be collected at 17.5 pips a month, but the widening that underpins both horizons' Factor 1 Bullish stance would be dead, removing +0.1944 tactically and +0.2025 strategically and taking the strategic score to -0.0555, i.e. mildly Bearish

invalidators.condition: VIX closes above 26 for three consecutive sessions or gold reclaims 4,600 on a sustained basis
invalidators.mechanism: EUR/CHF is the pair in which the base currency is explicitly not a haven and the quote currency explicitly is, so a genuine risk event is a double hit. At 3.77% three-month implied volatility the franc-funding book is carried at very high gearing and its exit is narrow, so the historical funding-unwind template of 3-4% in a fortnight (300-370 pips) applies and would erase more than eighteen months of carry. Factor 3 flips from Bullish to Bearish tactically, removing -0.1200 and taking the tactical score to +0.3509
invalidators.monitor_indicator: CBOE VIX daily close and XAU/USD

invalidators.condition: The OAT-Bund 10Y spread closes above 110bp, or a censure motion against the French government carries an absolute majority of 289 votes on or around 17 November
invalidators.mechanism: The franc is the only European currency that cannot be redenominated, so a revival of the redenomination premium that the TPI has never been tested against is mechanically a franc bid rather than merely a euro sale. Factor 8 would move from Bearish 65 to Bearish 85 and Factor 7 from Bearish 62 to Bearish 80, taking the strategic score from +0.1470 to roughly +0.1050 and then negative as Factor 3 follows on the flight-to-quality
invalidators.monitor_indicator: OAT-Bund 10Y spread and Assemblée nationale censure votes
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Daily for the spread; per vote for motions

invalidators.condition: Dutch TTF front-month gas sustains above EUR75/MWh for ten consecutive business days with EU storage below 70% on 1 November
invalidators.mechanism: Converts the energy shock from an inflation story that raises the ECB's path (pair-positive) into a euro-area balance-of-payments and growth shock (pair-negative), and Switzerland does not share the exposure. Factor 5 would move from Bearish 65 to Bearish 85, taking the strategic score from +0.1470 to +0.1150, and Factor 2 would turn Bearish as demand destruction dominates
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ICE Dutch TTF front-month settlement and GIE AGSI EU storage fill
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Daily for TTF, weekly for storage

invalidators.condition: The SNB revises its 2027 conditional inflation forecast above 1.0% at the 24 September or 10 December assessment, or removes the 'increased willingness to intervene' language
invalidators.mechanism: Both changes attack the pair's two structural supports simultaneously: an inflation revision above 1.0% restores the franc's policy optionality and validates the residual 12-25bp of front-end hawkishness, while removing the intervention pledge removes the one-directional official floor under the pair. Factor 6 would flip from Bullish 68/70 to Bearish, swinging the tactical score by -0.1224 and the strategic by -0.1960 (taking it to -0.0490)
invalidators.monitor_indicator: SNB assessment statement and conditional inflation forecast

invalidators.condition: EUR/CHF 3M implied volatility rises above 7.0% while spot is falling
invalidators.mechanism: At 3.77% the franc-funding trade is scalable and at 7.0% it is not — a near-doubling of implied volatility forces deleveraging of the position that is the pair's dominant flow, through an exit narrower than the position size implies. This is a pair-specific invalidator with no analogue in EUR/USD, because EUR/CHF's function as the market's lowest-volatility funding vehicle is entirely contingent on its volatility staying low
invalidators.monitor_indicator: EUR/CHF 3M ATM implied volatility alongside spot

signposts.indicator: ECB-SNB policy differential and September ECB hike probability
signposts.current_level: +225bp (ECB deposit 2.25%, SNB policy 0.00%); September hike probability 76.9-83%; cumulative probability of 2.25% by 17 December 91.9%
signposts.confirms_if: Hike probability holds above 75% into 10 September and the differential reaches 250bp on delivery
signposts.invalidates_if: Hike probability falls below 55%, or the ECB holds and revises 2027 HICP to 2.1% or below, capping the differential at 225bp permanently
signposts.bilateral_importance: This matters more for EUR/CHF than for any other euro cross because the quote leg is administratively frozen — the differential is the ECB's decision, with no offsetting move available. In EUR/USD the same information is diluted by a Fed with three hawkish dissenters; here it is undiluted.
signposts.frequency: Continuous; check daily around data releases and weekly otherwise

signposts.indicator: SNB sight deposits of domestic banks
signposts.current_level: CHF 442.66bn (week to 2026-07-24), up CHF 9.6bn (+2.2%) over three months; total sight deposits CHF 469.27bn
signposts.confirms_if: Flat to rising by up to CHF 5bn per four weeks; a rise above CHF 5bn in a fortnight is active franc selling and outright pair-bullish
signposts.invalidates_if: A fall of more than CHF 10bn over four weeks, indicating the SNB is selling reserves rather than accumulating them
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the SNB's operational instrument and it transacts in EUR/CHF, not USD/CHF — a sharp rise typically signals intervention and can move EUR/CHF on release. No other pair in the complex has a weekly official-sector flow indicator.

signposts.current_level: +2.5 percentage points (euro area 2.9% July flash vs Switzerland 0.4% July); core differential +2.2pp (2.5% vs 0.3%)
signposts.confirms_if: The differential holds at or above 2.4pp through the September and October releases
signposts.invalidates_if: The differential compresses below 1.5pp, requiring Swiss CPI at or above 1.0% with core above 0.6% alongside euro-area HICP below 2.5%
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the fundamental driver of the entire policy differential, and it is uniquely wide on this pair — no other G10 pair carries a 2.5pp inflation gap with a 225bp rate gap on top of it.
signposts.frequency: Monthly, both in the first days of each month

signposts.indicator: EUR/CHF 3M implied volatility and 25-delta risk reversal
signposts.confirms_if: 3M implied stays below 5.0% and the 1M risk reversal narrows toward -0.15 or better
signposts.invalidates_if: 3M implied rises above 7.0%, or the 1M risk reversal deepens beyond -0.60
signposts.bilateral_importance: EUR/CHF's function as the market's preferred low-volatility funding vehicle is entirely contingent on its own volatility staying low — this is the only pair in the G10 whose flow driver is a direct function of its own implied volatility.

signposts.current_level: 81-82bp (OAT 3.98%, Bund 3.15-3.17%), with the OAT at a 17-year high twice in July and the spread trading at or through BTP-Bund at 80-81bp
signposts.confirms_if: The spread narrows below 70bp, indicating the French budget process is being absorbed
signposts.invalidates_if: The spread widens through 110bp, reviving the redenomination premium
signposts.bilateral_importance: This matters more for EUR/CHF than for any other euro cross because the franc is the destination of European fiscal-stress capital flight and is the only European currency immune to redenomination risk — the pair therefore has higher beta to OAT-Bund than the euro index does.

signposts.confirms_if: The spread widens beyond 280bp, confirming that the euro leg's term-structure premium is expanding
signposts.invalidates_if: The spread compresses below 240bp, requiring either a Bund rally on a euro-area growth scare or a Swiss yield rise on SNB repricing
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the pair's term-structure carry and the widest positive spread the euro enjoys against any currency anywhere; it captures the fiscal and supply divergence that the policy-rate differential alone misses.

signposts.indicator: Gold (XAU/USD) as the franc's haven proxy
signposts.current_level: 4,054.45, down 12.14% over three months and 17.94% over six from a February peak of 5,277.88
signposts.confirms_if: Gold stays below 4,400, keeping the haven complex in drawdown
signposts.invalidates_if: Gold sustains a break above 4,600, signalling structural re-engagement of the haven complex
signposts.bilateral_importance: The franc and gold share a debasement-and-uncertainty demand function while the euro has no such linkage, which makes gold a purer read on this pair than the VIX — the 17.94% six-month drawdown has been worth roughly +1.0% to +1.4% of realised pair support.

signposts.indicator: EUR/CHF spot relative to the 50-day and 200-day moving averages
signposts.current_level: Spot 0.93244 vs 50-day 0.92534 (+0.77%), 100-day 0.92088 (+1.26%), 200-day 0.91835 (+1.53%); all three stacked bullishly with a golden cross completed in late July
signposts.confirms_if: Spot holds above the 50-day at 0.92534 on all daily closes
signposts.invalidates_if: A weekly close below the 200-day at 0.91835, flipping systematic and CTA capital from long-pair to short-pair
signposts.bilateral_importance: On a 3.4%-volatility pair, systematic trend flow is a proportionally larger share of total turnover than in higher-volatility majors, so MA-triggered flow moves this cross more than it moves EUR/USD — and the 200-day sits just below the six-month carry breakeven of 0.92194, meaning the technical and carry invalidations coincide within 36 pips.

assumptions: Spot, all performance figures, the 52-week range and percentile, all moving averages, the trend-regime assessment and the realised-volatility estimate are taken exclusively from the provided Twelve Data daily OHLC series (390 observations, 2025-06-12 to 2026-08-05), with spot at the 2026-08-05 close of 0.93244. This is four sessions after the stated valuation date of 2026-08-01; both dossiers carry EUR/CHF at 0.93166 and 0.9317 respectively for the 31 July close, and the SNB's own published fixing for 5 August is 0.9342. The 0.93244 figure is used throughout as the price-data source of truth; a 20-pip provenance difference does not change any stance.

Twenty-day realised volatility of approximately 3.5% annualised is computed by this analysis from the provided daily closes and is an estimate rather than a vendor print. The implied-volatility percentile is not computable from any free distribution and is stated as an estimate of roughly the 30th-40th percentile; this is flagged.

Support and resistance levels, chart patterns, implied volatilities, risk reversals, the vol term structure, bank forecasts and positioning commentary come exclusively from web research and are cited. Pair implied volatilities and risk reversals are carried from the franc dossier's Saxo snapshot dated 31 July 07:00 GMT; a 12:30 GMT re-fetch of the same live page returned different levels, so the levels carry intraday drift and are flagged.

EUR/CHF forward points and outright forwards were not retrievable as market quotes and are computed from covered interest parity using retrieved Euribor fixings against Swiss money-market rates anchored on the SARON fixing of -0.04% and assumed values for 3M and 6M. They exclude the cross-currency basis, which was unretrievable. The franc dossier establishes that USD/CHF forwards imply 34-49bp more franc appreciation than the policy gap alone; a similar wedge here would widen our stated edge rather than narrow it.

The 3M EUR/CHF and EUR/USD cross-currency basis levels — the framework's designated instrument for Factor 10 — could not be retrieved from any citable source, a gap both dossiers independently flag. Factor 10 is therefore assessed on indirect evidence and its confidence is capped at 58 tactical and 50 strategic for that reason. Any basis widening should be treated as a first-order invalidation signal this analysis cannot currently measure.

The OIS-derived SNB path underpinning the 'residual 12-25bp hawkish premium' claim is sourced from the franc dossier and carries a 2026-06-05 snapshot date, 57 days before the valuation date and outside both freshness windows. The claim is directionally corroborated by the near-unanimity of the SNB forecast consensus but the magnitude is not independently verifiable and is flagged.

Bilateral trade figures are taken directly from the injected IMF DOTS block (2024, USD) and are not re-estimated from the web, per instruction. The reporting asymmetry between the two directions is characteristic of Swiss trade statistics and reflects gold-refining and re-export flows; the euro-area-reported net surplus of $56.3bn is used as the headline bilateral figure.

Valuation is assessed on the relative-REER-differential method carried in both dossiers rather than on an absolute PPP dataset; the euro dossier's grid gives EUR/CHF fair value of 0.9261 and the franc dossier's mirror calculation 0.9227. Both are relative real-effective deviations from 30-month means, not absolute purchasing-power estimates, and neither can support a decade-length percentile because the cached BIS series carries only 30 monthly observations.
Weight adjustments are documented in the Weight Adjustments table, are each within the ±0.05 limit, and both columns sum to exactly 1.00. The rationale in each case is bilateral rather than generic.

Weighted scores are computed as stance score (Bullish +1, Neutral 0, Bearish -1) multiplied by confidence divided by 100, multiplied by the adjusted horizon weight, and summed. Score-to-conviction bands: absolute score below 0.10 = conviction 1; 0.10-0.25 = 2; 0.25-0.45 = 3; 0.45-0.55 = 4; above 0.55 = 5. Overall confidence is the weight-weighted average of the ten factor confidences at that horizon.

Factor stances are assessed fresh through a bilateral lens rather than derived by subtracting one dossier from the other. Where the resulting stance differs from a naive combination, it is stated explicitly — most importantly in Factor 1, Factor 2 and Factor 5.

Some cited sources are low-tier aggregators or technical-analysis desks rather than primary research. The Exchange Rates UK June 2026 bank survey pre-dates both the July ECB meeting and the tariff onset; the UBS 0.95 and Monex 0.96 targets derive from publications dated November 2025 and October 2025 respectively and are flagged as the oldest inputs in the consensus set. The blended model (0.9155-0.9185) is presented as evidence of consensus dispersion and is noted as already invalidated by spot.
